description: Guided Writing tasks with model answers and rubric checklists.

tasks.title: Reply to Jo's email about a weekend trip
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Jo. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
How are you? I'm planning a weekend trip to your town next month and I'm so excited!
Can you tell me the best way to get from the train station to your house? And what's the weather usually like this time of year?
I'd love to do something outdoors — do you have any ideas? Also, is there a good place where we could have dinner on Saturday evening?
Can't wait to see you!
Jo
points: Say how Jo can get from the station to your house
Recommend a place for dinner on Saturday
tasks.model:
Hi Jo,

Great to hear from you! I'm really looking forward to your visit.

The easiest way to my house is bus number 12 — it stops right outside the station, and you get off at Green Park. It takes about ten minutes.

The weather in May is usually warm and sunny, but it can rain a little, so bring a light jacket.

For something outdoors, how about cycling around the lake? We can rent bikes cheaply near the park.

On Saturday evening, let's eat at Luigi's — the best pizza in town!

See you soon!

Maria
tasks.modelNotes: Notice how each of the four content points gets its own short paragraph, the opening is friendly and warm, and it closes with 'See you soon'. Range structure: 'how about cycling' (suggestion) and 'looking forward to + -ing'.
checklist: All four content points are answered
The email opens and closes politely
There is at least one suggestion (why don't we / how about)
Linking words connect the ideas (and, but, so, because)
About 100 words

tasks.title: Reply to Ben's email about learning English
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Ben. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
Thanks for your last email. I have some news — I'm coming to study in your country for three months this autumn!
I want to improve my English before I arrive. How do you usually learn new words? Do you think watching films in English is a good idea?
Also, what should I bring with me for the first week? I don't want to carry too much.
And could you introduce me to some of your friends before I come?
Write soon!
Ben
points: Explain how you usually learn new words
Give your opinion about watching English films
Say what Ben should bring for the first week
Answer his question about meeting friends
tasks.model:
Hi Ben,

Thanks for your email — what fantastic news! Three months here will be amazing.

I usually learn new words by writing them in a small notebook and using them in sentences. It really works!

I think watching English films is a great idea, especially with English subtitles. You'll hear natural, everyday language.

For the first week, don't bring too much — just comfortable shoes, a warm jacket and something nice to wear when you meet people.

Of course I'll introduce you to my friends! I'm looking forward to showing you around.

Best wishes,
Lena
tasks.modelNotes: Every content point is answered in order. 'I think ... is a great idea' gives an opinion, and 'looking forward to showing' adds range.
checklist: All four content points are answered
An opinion is clearly given about films
Advice uses should / don't + verb
The tone is friendly, not formal
About 100 words

tasks.title: Article: My favourite place in my town
tasks.rubric: An English website asks readers to write articles about their favourite places. Write your article (about 100 words), saying where the place is, what people can do there, and why you like it.
points: Describe what people can do there
tasks.model:
The Old Harbour

Have you ever found a place that feels like another world? For me, that place is the Old Harbour in the south of my town.

In the morning, you can watch the fishing boats coming in, and at weekends there is a small market with local food. Many people walk along the sea wall or sit in the little cafés.

I love it because it is peaceful and beautiful, especially at sunset. The colours are so wonderful that I have taken hundreds of photos there.

If you visit my town, you should certainly go to the Old Harbour. You won't forget it!
tasks.modelNotes: The article opens with a question to the reader, organises ideas into clear paragraphs, and uses 'so ... that' — a range structure. It ends with a direct recommendation.
checklist: The article has a title
It speaks to the reader (question / you)
Ideas are organised in paragraphs
There is at least one range structure (so...that, not only...but also)
About 100 words

tasks.title: Story: A surprise at the station
tasks.rubric: Your teacher has asked you to write a story with the title 'A surprise at the station'. Write your story (about 100 words).
points: Set the scene at a station
tasks.model:
A Surprise at the Station

It was a rainy Friday afternoon, and I was waiting for the train to visit my grandmother. The platform was crowded, and everyone looked tired.

Suddenly, I heard someone calling my name. I turned around — and I couldn't believe my eyes. It was my cousin Tom, who lives in Australia! I hadn't seen him for five years.

He laughed and explained that he had arrived that morning to surprise the family. We talked and talked until my train came.

In the end, I missed my train — but I didn't care. It was the best surprise of my life.
tasks.modelNotes: The story sets the scene with past tenses (was waiting / was crowded), builds the moment with 'suddenly', and closes with a feeling. Sequence words: suddenly, in the end.
checklist: The title is included
The scene is set with past tenses
There is a clear surprise/problem and a resolution
Sequence words are used (suddenly, then, in the end)
About 100 words
